summary.en: King Jangsu of Goguryeo raised a 6-metre stone stele near the capital Gungnae (modern Ji'an) to commemorate his father Gwanggaeto. Its roughly 1,800 characters record the dynasty's origins and Gwanggaeto's campaigns and are a key source for early relations between Goguryeo, Baekje, Silla and Wa.
summary.zh: 高句丽长寿王在国内城（今集安）附近立起高约六米的石碑，纪念其父广开土王。碑文约一千八百字，记述王室起源与广开土王的征战，是研究高句丽、百济、新罗与倭早期关系的重要史料。

sources.title: Gwanggaeto Stele inscription (414)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Capital Cities and Tombs of the Ancient Koguryo Kingdom
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Gwanggaeto Stele

summary.en: Goguryeo general Eulji Mundeok lured a large Sui expeditionary force deep into the peninsula and destroyed it as it retreated across the Salsu (probably the Cheongcheon River). The disaster crippled Emperor Yang's campaigns against Goguryeo.
summary.zh: 高句丽将领乙支文德诱使隋朝远征大军深入，并在其撤退渡过萨水（一般认为即清川江）时予以重创。此役使隋炀帝征讨高句丽的战争严重受挫。

sources.title: Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Suishu (Book of Sui, 636), annals of Emperor Yang
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Battle of Salsu

note: Wikidata gives no coordinates; the Salsu is usually identified with the Cheongcheon River near Anju, and Sui troop numbers in the sources are probably exaggerated.

summary.en: A set of moral and political injunctions for officials, drawing on Confucian and Buddhist ideals, which the Nihon Shoki attributes to Prince Shōtoku in 604. It stresses harmony, reverence for Buddhism and obedience to the sovereign.
summary.zh: 据《日本书纪》记载，圣德太子于604年制定了这一针对官员的道德与政治训诫，融合儒家与佛教思想，强调“以和为贵”、崇敬佛法、服从君主。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Seventeen-article constitution
Nihon Shoki (720), trans. W. G. Aston, Nihongi (1896)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 1: Ancient Japan (1993)
Wikipedia: Seventeen-article constitution

note: Known only from the Nihon Shoki (720); its date and Shōtoku's authorship are debated by historians.

summary.en: After the overthrow of the Soga clan in 645, Prince Naka no Ōe and Nakatomi no Kamatari launched reforms under Emperor Kōtoku modelled on Tang China: land and people were declared the sovereign's, and a centralised bureaucracy and tax system were planned from the new palace at Naniwa.
summary.zh: 645年苏我氏被推翻后，中大兄皇子与中臣镰足在孝德天皇治下仿效唐朝推行改革，宣布土地与人民归于天皇，并以难波新宫为中心筹划中央集权的官僚与税制。

sources.title: Nihon Shoki (720), trans. W. G. Aston, Nihongi (1896)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 1: Ancient Japan (1993)
Wikipedia: Taika Reform

note: The wording of the 646 reform edict in the Nihon Shoki was probably revised later; the real pace of reform is debated.

name.en: Battle of Hwangsanbeol and fall of Baekje
name.zh: 黄山伐之战与百济灭亡

summary.en: Baekje general Gyebaek made a last stand against the Silla army of Kim Yu-sin at Hwangsanbeol while a Tang fleet landed in the west. The Baekje capital Sabi fell soon after and King Uija surrendered.
summary.zh: 百济将领阶伯在黄山伐迎战金庾信率领的新罗军，最终战死，同时唐朝水军在西海岸登陆。不久百济都城泗沘陷落，义慈王投降。

sources.title: Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Battle of Hwangsanbeol

note: Battlefield location near Nonsan is approximate (Wikidata gives none).

summary.en: A Yamato fleet sent to restore Baekje was destroyed by Tang and Silla naval forces at the mouth of the Baekgang (Geum River). The defeat ended Baekje restoration hopes and led Japan to fortify its western coasts.
summary.zh: 倭国派遣水军援助百济复国，在白江口（今锦江入海口）被唐朝与新罗联军击败。此役终结了百济复国的希望，也促使日本在西部沿海修筑防御工事。

sources.title: Nihon Shoki (720), trans. W. G. Aston, Nihongi (1896)
Jiu Tangshu (Old Book of Tang, 945), "Biography of Liu Rengui" and "Account of Baekje"
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Battle of Baekgang

name.en: Goguryeo–Tang War and fall of Pyongyang
name.zh: 唐与高句丽战争及平壤陷落

summary.en: After repeated Tang invasions from 645, an allied Tang–Silla army besieged Pyongyang in 668 and captured King Bojang, ending Goguryeo after some seven centuries. Tang set up the Protectorate General to Pacify the East in its former capital.
summary.zh: 唐朝自645年起多次进攻高句丽，668年唐与新罗联军围攻平壤，俘获宝藏王，高句丽灭亡。唐朝随后在平壤设立安东都护府。

sources.title: Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Goguryeo–Tang War

summary.en: Having helped Tang destroy Baekje and Goguryeo, Silla turned on its ally when Tang tried to rule the peninsula directly. Victories at Maeso fortress (675) and Gibeolpo (676) forced Tang to withdraw, leaving Silla master of the peninsula south of the Taedong River.
summary.zh: 新罗协助唐朝灭百济与高句丽后，因唐欲直接统治半岛而与之反目。675年买肖城之战与676年伎伐浦海战获胜后，唐军撤退，新罗控制了大同江以南的半岛。

sources.title: Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Silla–Tang War

summary.en: Empress Genmei moved the court to Heijō-kyō (Nara), a grid-planned capital modelled on Tang Chang'an. It gave its name to the Nara period and, apart from 740–745, remained the capital until 784.
summary.zh: 元明天皇将都城迁至仿照唐长安城棋盘式规划的平城京（今奈良）。奈良时代因此得名，除740至745年外，此地一直为都城，直至784年。

sources.title: Shoku Nihongi (797)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic Monuments of Ancient Nara
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 1: Ancient Japan (1993)
Wikipedia: Heijō-kyō

summary.en: Ō no Yasumaro presented the Kojiki, Japan's oldest surviving chronicle, to Empress Genmei. It narrates the creation myths and the genealogy of the imperial line up to Empress Suiko.
summary.zh: 太安万侣向元明天皇献上《古事记》，这是现存最古老的日本史书，记述了创世神话及至推古天皇为止的皇室谱系。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Kojiki
Donald L. Philippi (trans.), Kojiki (University of Tokyo Press, 1968)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 1: Ancient Japan (1993)
Wikipedia: Kojiki

summary.en: Emperor Shōmu's colossal bronze Vairocana Buddha at Tōdai-ji, the head temple of the provincial temple network, was ceremonially "eye-opened" in 752 before monks from across Asia.
summary.zh: 圣武天皇下令铸造的东大寺卢舍那大佛于752年举行开眼供养法会，来自亚洲各地的僧侣参加。东大寺是全国国分寺体系的总寺。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Tōdai Temple
Shoku Nihongi (797)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic Monuments of Ancient Nara
Wikipedia: Tōdai-ji

summary.en: According to the Samguk yusa, the Silla minister Kim Dae-seong began the artificial granite grotto of Seokguram on Mount Toham in 751, together with Bulguksa temple below. Its seated Buddha is a masterpiece of East Asian Buddhist sculpture.
summary.zh: 据《三国遗事》记载，新罗宰相金大城于751年在吐含山开始营建人工花岗岩石窟石窟庵，并同时修建山下的佛国寺。窟内本尊坐佛是东亚佛教雕塑的杰作。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Sokkuram
Iryeon, Samguk yusa (Memorabilia of the Three Kingdoms, c. 1281)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Seokguram Grotto and Bulguksa Temple
Wikipedia: Seokguram

note: The 751 start and 774 completion follow the Samguk yusa.

summary.en: Emperor Kanmu moved the court from Nagaoka to the new grid-planned capital of Heian-kyō, modern Kyoto. It remained the imperial capital until 1869 and gave its name to the Heian period.
summary.zh: 桓武天皇将朝廷从长冈京迁至新建的棋盘式都城平安京，即今京都。此后直到1869年这里一直是天皇所在的都城，平安时代亦由此得名。

sources.title: The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 2: Heian Japan (1999)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto (Kyoto, Uji and Otsu Cities)
Wikipedia: Heian-kyō

name.en: Later Three Kingdoms and Goryeo reunification
name.zh: 后三国时代与高丽统一

summary.en: As Silla weakened, rebel states Later Baekje and Taebong (Later Goguryeo) arose. Wang Geon, who founded Goryeo in 918, accepted Silla's surrender in 935 and defeated Later Baekje at Illicheon in 936, reuniting the peninsula.
summary.zh: 新罗衰落后，后百济与泰封（后高句丽）相继崛起。918年建立高丽的王建于935年接受新罗归降，936年在一利川击败后百济，重新统一朝鲜半岛。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Later Three Kingdoms
Kim Bu-sik, Samguk sagi (History of the Three Kingdoms, 1145)
Goryeosa (History of Goryeo, 1451)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Later Three Kingdoms

summary.en: Murasaki Shikibu, a lady-in-waiting at the Heian court, wrote this long prose narrative of the life and loves of the "Shining Prince" Genji. It was circulating by 1008 and is often called the world's first novel.
summary.zh: 平安宫廷女官紫式部创作了这部描写“光源氏”一生与情爱的长篇物语。至1008年该书已在宫中流传，常被誉为世界上第一部长篇小说。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: The Tale of Genji
Murasaki Shikibu, Murasaki Shikibu nikki (Diary, c. 1010)
Richard Bowring, Murasaki Shikibu: The Tale of Genji (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2004)
Wikipedia: The Tale of Genji

note: Wikidata gives 1010 as inception; the earliest datable reference to the work, in Murasaki's diary, is from 1008. Composition dates are not known precisely.

summary.en: From 1231 the Mongols invaded Goryeo repeatedly. The military regime moved the court to Ganghwa Island and resisted for decades while the mainland was ravaged, until Goryeo accepted vassal status in 1259.
summary.zh: 自1231年起蒙古多次入侵高丽。武臣政权将朝廷迁往江华岛，坚持抵抗数十年，本土则惨遭蹂躏，直至1259年高丽接受藩属地位。

sources.title: Goryeosa (History of Goryeo, 1451)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Mongol invasions of Korea

summary.en: During the Mongol invasions Goryeo carved the entire Buddhist canon onto more than 81,000 woodblocks, hoping for divine protection. Carved under the court in exile on Ganghwa Island and completed in 1251, the blocks were moved to Haeinsa temple in 1398, where they remain.
summary.zh: 蒙古入侵期间，高丽为祈求佛法护国，将整部大藏经刻于八万一千余块木板之上，由江华岛流亡朝廷主持，1251年完成，1398年移藏海印寺至今。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Tripitaka Koreana
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Haeinsa Temple Janggyeong Panjeon, the Depositories for the Tripitaka Koreana Woodblocks
Goryeosa (History of Goryeo, 1451)
Wikipedia: Tripitaka Koreana

note: Wikidata gives an inception of 1300; standard accounts date the carving to 1236/37–1251.

summary.en: A civil war between the Taira and Minamoto warrior clans. It ended with the destruction of the Taira fleet at Dan-no-ura in 1185 and left Minamoto no Yoritomo the dominant power in Japan.
summary.zh: 平氏与源氏两大武士集团之间的内战。1185年平氏水军在坛之浦覆灭，源赖朝由此成为日本最有权势的人物。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Genpei War
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 3: Medieval Japan (1990)
Azuma kagami (Mirror of the East, late 13th c.)
Wikipedia: Genpei War

summary.en: Minamoto no Yoritomo, already ruling the warrior class from Kamakura, was appointed sei-i taishōgun in 1192. His government created a dual system in which the shogunate controlled military affairs alongside the imperial court in Kyoto.
summary.zh: 已在镰仓统领武士阶层的源赖朝于1192年被任命为征夷大将军。幕府掌握军事与地方治安，与京都朝廷并存，形成公武二元体制。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Kamakura shogunate
Azuma kagami (Mirror of the East, late 13th c.)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 3: Medieval Japan (1990)
Wikipedia: Kamakura shogunate

note: Historians date the regime variously from 1180, 1185 or 1192; Wikidata gives 1200. No Wikidata item exists for this event itself; Q736839 denotes the state and is linked from polity-kamakura, so no qid is set here.

summary.en: Kublai Khan's Yuan dynasty, with Goryeo ships and troops, twice invaded northern Kyushu. Both attacks at Hakata Bay were contained by samurai defenders (in 1281 also by the new coastal wall), and storms—later called kamikaze—wrecked much of the 1281 fleet.
summary.zh: 忽必烈的元朝联合高丽船只与兵力两次进攻九州北部。两次在博多湾的登陆都被武士阻挡（1281年另有新筑的石垒），1281年的庞大舰队更多被台风（后称“神风”）摧毁。

label.en: Battle of Bun'ei at Hakata Bay

label.zh: 江南军自庆元（宁波）出发

label.en: Battle of Kōan at Hakata Bay

label.zh: 台风在鹰岛海域摧毁舰队

sources.title: Thomas D. Conlan, In Little Need of Divine Intervention: Takezaki Suenaga's Scrolls of the Mongol Invasions of Japan (Cornell, 2001)
Yuanshi (History of Yuan, 1370), "Account of Japan" (Riben zhuan)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 3: Medieval Japan (1990)
Wikipedia: Mongol invasions of Japan

name.zh: 《直指心体要节》金属活字印刷

summary.en: Monks at Heungdeok temple in Cheongju printed this anthology of Seon (Zen) teachings with movable metal type. The surviving volume, held in the Bibliothèque nationale de France, is the oldest extant book printed this way.
summary.zh: 清州兴德寺僧人用金属活字印行这部禅宗语录选集。现存的一卷藏于法国国家图书馆，是世界上现存最早的金属活字印本。

sources.title: UNESCO Memory of the World Register: Baegun hwasang chorok buljo jikji simche yojeol (vol. II)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Jikji

summary.en: General Yi Seong-gye, who had turned his army back at Wihwa Island in 1388 and taken power, deposed the last Goryeo king and was enthroned as King Taejo in Gaegyeong. He renamed the state Joseon and moved the capital to Hanseong (Seoul) in 1394.
summary.zh: 1388年威化岛回军后掌握大权的将军李成桂，于1392年废黜高丽末代国王，在开京即位为太祖。他改国号为朝鲜，并于1394年迁都汉城（今首尔）。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Chosŏn dynasty
Annals of the Joseon Dynasty (Joseon wangjo sillok), National Institute of Korean History
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Joseon

note: No Wikidata item exists for this event itself; Q28179 denotes the state and is linked from polity-joseon, so no qid is set here.

summary.en: King Sejong completed a new phonetic alphabet in 1443 and promulgated it in 1446 in the document Hunminjeongeum, "the correct sounds for instructing the people", so that commoners could read and write Korean.
summary.zh: 世宗大王于1443年创制了一套新的表音文字，并于1446年以《训民正音》（意为“教百姓以正确的字音”）颁布，使平民也能读写朝鲜语。

sources.title: Annals of the Joseon Dynasty (Joseon wangjo sillok), National Institute of Korean History
UNESCO Memory of the World Register: Hunmin Chongum Manuscript
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Hunminjeongeum

summary.en: A succession dispute in the Ashikaga shogunate drew the Hosokawa and Yamana coalitions into a decade of fighting that burned much of Kyoto. The shogunate never recovered its authority, opening the Sengoku (Warring States) era.
summary.zh: 足利将军家的继嗣纷争使细川与山名两大阵营在京都激战十年，城市大半焚毁。幕府权威一蹶不振，日本由此进入战国时代。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Ōnin War
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 3: Medieval Japan (1990)
Conrad Totman, A History of Japan (Blackwell, 2nd ed. 2005)
Wikipedia: Ōnin War

note: Coordinates set on Kyoto, where the fighting took place; the Wikidata point lies about 17 km to the south.

summary.en: Oda Nobunaga, with a small force, surprised and killed the daimyō Imagawa Yoshimoto, whose much larger army was marching through Owari. The victory launched Nobunaga's rise as a unifier of Japan.
summary.zh: 织田信长以少量兵力奇袭行军经过尾张的今川义元大军，并斩杀义元。此役使信长崛起，开始统一日本的进程。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Okehazama
Jeroen P. Lamers, Japonius Tyrannus: The Japanese Warlord Oda Nobunaga Reconsidered (Hotei, 2000)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 4: Early Modern Japan (1991)
Wikipedia: Battle of Okehazama

name.zh: 壬辰倭乱（万历朝鲜战争）

summary.en: Toyotomi Hideyoshi sent some 150,000 troops into Joseon in 1592, aiming ultimately at Ming China. After rapid Japanese advances, Ming intervention, guerrilla resistance and Yi Sun-sin's navy stalled the campaign; a second invasion in 1597 ended with Hideyoshi's death and withdrawal in 1598.
summary.zh: 1592年丰臣秀吉派遣约十五万大军入侵朝鲜，最终目标是明朝。日军初期推进迅速，但明军援朝、义兵抗击与李舜臣水军使战事陷入僵局；1597年再度入侵，1598年秀吉死后日军撤退。

label.zh: 肥前名护屋城：出兵基地

label.en: Yi Sun-sin wins at Hansan Island

sources.title: Kenneth M. Swope, A Dragon's Head and a Serpent's Tail: Ming China and the First Great East Asian War, 1592–1598 (University of Oklahoma Press, 2009)
Stephen Turnbull, Samurai Invasion: Japan's Korean War 1592–98 (Cassell, 2002)
Yu Seong-ryong, Jingbirok (Book of Corrections, c. 1604)
Wikipedia: Imjin War

summary.en: Admiral Yi Sun-sin lured a Japanese fleet into open water near Hansan Island and enveloped it in a "crane-wing" formation, sinking or capturing most of the ships. The victory cut Japanese sea supply along Korea's southern coast.
summary.zh: 李舜臣将日本舰队诱至闲山岛附近的开阔海域，以“鹤翼阵”合围，击沉或俘获大部分敌船。此役切断了日军沿朝鲜南海岸的海上补给线。

sources.title: Yi Sun-sin, Nanjung ilgi (War Diary, 1592–1598)
Stephen Turnbull, Samurai Invasion: Japan's Korean War 1592–98 (Cassell, 2002)
Wikipedia: Battle of Hansan Island

summary.en: With only 13 warships left after the Joseon navy's disaster at Chilcheollyang, Yi Sun-sin used the fierce tidal currents of the Myeongnyang Strait to repel a Japanese fleet many times larger, halting the Japanese advance by sea.
summary.zh: 朝鲜水军在漆川梁惨败后，李舜臣仅余十三艘战船，他利用鸣梁海峡湍急的潮流，击退数倍于己的日本舰队，阻止了日军的海上推进。

sources.title: Yi Sun-sin, Nanjung ilgi (War Diary, 1592–1598)
Kenneth M. Swope, A Dragon's Head and a Serpent's Tail: Ming China and the First Great East Asian War, 1592–1598 (University of Oklahoma Press, 2009)
Wikipedia: Battle of Myeongnyang

summary.en: Tokugawa Ieyasu's Eastern Army defeated the Western Army led by Ishida Mitsunari, helped by defections during the battle. The victory made Ieyasu master of Japan; he became shogun in 1603.
summary.zh: 德川家康率领的东军在战场倒戈的帮助下击败石田三成为首的西军。此役使家康成为日本实际的统治者，并于1603年就任征夷大将军。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Sekigahara
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 4: Early Modern Japan (1991)
Conrad Totman, A History of Japan (Blackwell, 2nd ed. 2005)
Wikipedia: Battle of Sekigahara

summary.en: In two winter and summer campaigns the Tokugawa besieged Osaka Castle, the last stronghold of Toyotomi Hideyori. Its fall in 1615 destroyed the Toyotomi line and secured Tokugawa rule for two and a half centuries.
summary.zh: 德川方分冬、夏两阵围攻丰臣秀赖的最后据点大坂城。1615年城陷，丰臣氏灭亡，德川统治由此稳固了两个半世纪。

sources.title: The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 4: Early Modern Japan (1991)
Conrad Totman, A History of Japan (Blackwell, 2nd ed. 2005)
Wikipedia: Siege of Osaka

summary.en: Overtaxed peasants and masterless samurai of Shimabara and Amakusa, many of them Christian, rose and held Hara Castle until it fell to a shogunal army in 1638. The revolt hardened the ban on Christianity and the exclusion of the Portuguese.
summary.zh: 岛原与天草地区不堪重税的农民和浪人（多为天主教徒）起事，据守原城，1638年被幕府大军攻陷。此后幕府更加严厉地禁教，并驱逐葡萄牙人。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Shimabara Rebellion
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 4: Early Modern Japan (1991)
Ronald P. Toby, State and Diplomacy in Early Modern Japan (Princeton University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Shimabara Rebellion

summary.en: A series of Tokugawa edicts in the 1630s banned Japanese from travelling abroad, expelled the Portuguese and confined Dutch trade to Dejima in Nagasaki. Controlled contacts continued with China, Korea, the Ryukyus and the Ainu until the 1850s.
summary.zh: 17世纪30年代德川幕府颁布一系列法令，禁止日本人出海、驱逐葡萄牙人，并将荷兰贸易限制在长崎出岛。与中国、朝鲜、琉球及阿伊努的有限往来则一直持续到19世纪50年代。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: sakoku
Ronald P. Toby, State and Diplomacy in Early Modern Japan (Princeton University Press, 1984)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 4: Early Modern Japan (1991)
Wikipedia: Sakoku

note: The term sakoku was coined only in 1801; historians debate how closed Japan really was.

summary.en: US Commodore Matthew Perry anchored his "black ships" off Uraga in 1853 and returned in 1854 to obtain the Convention of Kanagawa, which opened two ports to American ships and ended Japan's policy of seclusion.
summary.zh: 1853年美国海军准将佩里率“黑船”驶抵浦贺，1854年再次来航，迫使幕府签订《神奈川条约》，开放两个港口供美国船只停靠，日本锁国政策就此终结。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Perry Expedition
Francis L. Hawks, Narrative of the Expedition of an American Squadron to the China Seas and Japan (1856)
Marius B. Jansen, The Making of Modern Japan (Harvard University Press, 2000)
Wikipedia: Perry Expedition

summary.en: Samurai from Satsuma and Chōshū proclaimed the restoration of imperial rule in Kyoto on 3 January 1868 and defeated the shogunate in the Boshin War. The new government abolished the domains and samurai privileges and set Japan on a course of rapid modernisation.
summary.zh: 1868年1月3日，萨摩、长州等藩的武士在京都宣布“王政复古”，并在戊辰战争中击败幕府。新政府废藩置县、废除武士特权，使日本走上迅速现代化的道路。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Meiji Restoration
Marius B. Jansen, The Making of Modern Japan (Harvard University Press, 2000)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 5: The Nineteenth Century (1989)
Wikipedia: Meiji Restoration

summary.en: After a gunboat confrontation off Ganghwa Island, Japan forced Joseon to sign its first modern, unequal treaty, opening three ports and granting Japanese extraterritoriality. It ended Korea's seclusion and its exclusive tributary ties to Qing China.
summary.zh: 在江华岛炮舰冲突之后，日本迫使朝鲜签订第一个近代不平等条约，开放三处港口并给予日本领事裁判权。条约打破了朝鲜的闭关状态及其与清朝的宗藩关系。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Treaty of Ganghwa
Peter Duus, The Abacus and the Sword: The Japanese Penetration of Korea, 1895–1910 (University of California Press, 1995)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Japan–Korea Treaty of 1876

name.zh: 东学农民运动（甲午农民战争）

summary.en: Peasants led by followers of the Donghak religion rose against corrupt officials in Jeolla province in 1894. The Joseon court's appeal for Qing troops prompted Japan to send its own, triggering the First Sino-Japanese War; the rebels were crushed by early 1895.
summary.zh: 1894年，东学道信徒领导全罗道农民反抗贪官污吏。朝鲜朝廷请求清军援助，日本亦借机出兵，引发甲午中日战争；起义军于1895年初被镇压。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Donghak Peasant Revolution
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: Tonghak Peasant Revolution

summary.en: Rivalry over Manchuria and Korea led Japan to attack the Russian fleet at Port Arthur in 1904. Japanese victories on land at Mukden and at sea at Tsushima produced the Treaty of Portsmouth, the first defeat of a European great power by an Asian state in modern times.
summary.zh: 日俄两国因争夺中国东北与朝鲜而交恶，1904年日本突袭旅顺口的俄国舰队。日本在奉天陆战与对马海战中获胜，双方签订《朴次茅斯条约》，这是近代亚洲国家首次击败欧洲列强。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Russo-Japanese War
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 6: The Twentieth Century (1988)
Marius B. Jansen, The Making of Modern Japan (Harvard University Press, 2000)
Wikipedia: Russo-Japanese War

summary.en: Admiral Tōgō Heihachirō's fleet annihilated the Russian Baltic Fleet, which had sailed halfway around the world, in the Tsushima Strait. The battle decided the Russo-Japanese War.
summary.zh: 东乡平八郎率领的日本联合舰队在对马海峡全歼远航半个地球而来的俄国波罗的海舰队，决定了日俄战争的结局。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Battle of Tsushima
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 6: The Twentieth Century (1988)
Marius B. Jansen, The Making of Modern Japan (Harvard University Press, 2000)
Wikipedia: Battle of Tsushima

summary.en: Under military pressure, Korean ministers signed a treaty making the Korean Empire a Japanese protectorate and handing its diplomacy to a Japanese Resident-General, Itō Hirobumi. Emperor Gojong never ratified it.
summary.zh: 在日本军事压力下，大韩帝国大臣签订条约，使韩国沦为日本保护国，外交权交由日本统监伊藤博文掌管。高宗皇帝始终未予批准。

sources.title: Peter Duus, The Abacus and the Sword: The Japanese Penetration of Korea, 1895–1910 (University of California Press, 1995)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Japan–Korea Treaty of 1905

summary.en: Prime Minister Yi Wan-yong and Resident-General Terauchi Masatake signed the annexation treaty on 22 August 1910; it was proclaimed a week later, ending the Korean Empire and beginning 35 years of Japanese colonial rule.
summary.zh: 1910年8月22日，总理大臣李完用与统监寺内正毅签订合并条约，一周后公布。大韩帝国就此灭亡，朝鲜开始了长达三十五年的日本殖民统治。

sources.title: Peter Duus, The Abacus and the Sword: The Japanese Penetration of Korea, 1895–1910 (University of California Press, 1995)
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Wikipedia: Japan–Korea Treaty of 1910

summary.en: A Declaration of Independence was read in Seoul on 1 March 1919, sparking nationwide peaceful demonstrations against Japanese rule. Their violent suppression killed thousands, but the movement led to the Korean Provisional Government in Shanghai.
summary.zh: 1919年3月1日，《独立宣言》在汉城宣读，引发全国性反对日本统治的和平示威。运动遭血腥镇压，数千人遇难，但随后促成了上海大韩民国临时政府的成立。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: March First Movement
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
Ki-baik Lee, A New History of Korea (Harvard University Press, 1984)
Wikipedia: March First Movement

summary.en: A magnitude 7.9 earthquake beneath Sagami Bay struck at midday, and the fires that followed destroyed much of Tokyo and Yokohama. More than 100,000 people died, and in the chaos vigilantes massacred thousands of Koreans.
summary.zh: 一场约7.9级地震在相模湾下方于正午发生，随后的大火焚毁了东京和横滨的大部分地区，死亡逾十万人。混乱中，自警团屠杀了数千名朝鲜人。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Great Kantō earthquake
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 6: The Twentieth Century (1988)
Conrad Totman, A History of Japan (Blackwell, 2nd ed. 2005)
Wikipedia: Great Kantō Earthquake

summary.en: The US B-29 Enola Gay dropped the uranium bomb "Little Boy" on Hiroshima, the first use of a nuclear weapon in war. Around 70,000–80,000 people died instantly and many more by the end of 1945.
summary.zh: 美国B-29轰炸机“艾诺拉·盖”号在广岛投下铀弹“小男孩”，这是核武器首次用于战争。约七万至八万人当场死亡，至1945年底死亡人数大幅增加。

sources.title: U.S. Strategic Bombing Survey, The Effects of Atomic Bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki (1946)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Hiroshima Peace Memorial (Genbaku Dome)
Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum
Wikipedia: Atomic bombing of Hiroshima

summary.en: Three days after Hiroshima, the plutonium bomb "Fat Man" exploded over the Urakami district of Nagasaki, killing some 40,000 people immediately. Japan announced its surrender on 15 August.
summary.zh: 广岛原爆三天后，钚弹“胖子”在长崎浦上地区上空爆炸，约四万人当场死亡。8月15日日本宣布投降。

sources.title: U.S. Strategic Bombing Survey, The Effects of Atomic Bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki (1946)
The Cambridge History of Japan, Vol. 6: The Twentieth Century (1988)
Wikipedia: Atomic bombing of Nagasaki

summary.en: North Korea invaded the South in June 1950. A US-led UN force, after holding the Pusan Perimeter and landing at Incheon, advanced to the Yalu; Chinese intervention drove it back, and the front settled near the 38th parallel until the 1953 armistice.
summary.zh: 1950年6月朝鲜人民军南下。以美国为首的联合国军守住釜山防御圈并在仁川登陆后推进至鸭绿江；中国人民志愿军参战后将其击退，战线最终稳定在三八线附近，直至1953年签订停战协定。

label.en: North Korean forces cross the 38th parallel (25 June)
label.zh: 朝鲜人民军越过三八线（6月25日）
联合国军推进至鸭绿江

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Korean War
Bruce Cumings, The Korean War: A History (Modern Library, 2010)
Roy E. Appleman, South to the Naktong, North to the Yalu (U.S. Army Center of Military History, 1961)
Wikipedia: Korean War

summary.en: General Douglas MacArthur's amphibious landing at Incheon, behind North Korean lines, led to the recapture of Seoul and the collapse of the North Korean army in the South.
summary.zh: 麦克阿瑟将军指挥联合国军在朝鲜人民军后方的仁川实施两栖登陆，随后收复汉城，使南下的朝鲜人民军全面溃退。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Incheon landing
Roy E. Appleman, South to the Naktong, North to the Yalu (U.S. Army Center of Military History, 1961)
Bruce Cumings, The Korean War: A History (Modern Library, 2010)
Wikipedia: Battle of Inchon

summary.en: Signed at Panmunjom by the UN Command, the Korean People's Army and the Chinese People's Volunteers, the armistice ended fighting and created the Demilitarized Zone. No peace treaty has followed.
summary.zh: 联合国军司令部与朝鲜人民军、中国人民志愿军在板门店签署停战协定，停止敌对行动并设立非军事区。此后双方至今未签订和平条约。

sources.title: Bruce Cumings, The Korean War: A History (Modern Library, 2010)
Roy E. Appleman, South to the Naktong, North to the Yalu (U.S. Army Center of Military History, 1961)
Wikipedia: Korean Armistice Agreement

summary.en: The 24th Summer Olympics, held in Seoul shortly after South Korea's transition to democracy, showcased the country's rapid industrialisation and brought together athletes from both Cold War blocs after two boycotted Games.
summary.zh: 第24届夏季奥运会在韩国民主化转型后不久于汉城举行，展示了韩国迅速工业化的成就，也是在两届遭抵制的奥运会之后东西方阵营运动员再度同场竞技。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Seoul Summer Olympics
Michael J. Seth, A History of Korea: From Antiquity to the Present (Rowman & Littlefield, 2010)
International Olympic Committee: Seoul 1988
Wikipedia: 1988 Summer Olympics

summary.en: A magnitude 9.0–9.1 megathrust earthquake off northeastern Honshu generated a tsunami that killed about 18,000 people and caused meltdowns at the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear plant.
summary.zh: 本州东北近海发生9.0至9.1级逆冲型大地震，引发海啸，约一万八千人罹难，并导致福岛第一核电站发生堆芯熔毁。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami
Japan Meteorological Agency, The 2011 off the Pacific coast of Tohoku Earthquake (report, 2011)
USGS: M 9.1 – 2011 Great Tohoku Earthquake, Japan
Wikipedia: 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami

summary.en: King Seong of Baekje sent a gilt-bronze Buddha image and sutras to the Yamato court of Emperor Kinmei. The Soga clan championed the new faith against the Mononobe and Nakatomi; after the Soga victory in 587, Buddhism became a pillar of the Asuka state.
summary.zh: 百济圣王向钦明天皇的大和朝廷献上金铜佛像和经论。苏我氏支持这一新信仰，与物部氏和中臣氏对立；587年苏我氏获胜后，佛教成为飞鸟时代国家的支柱。

sources.title: 《日本书纪》卷第十九 钦明天皇十三年（维基文库）
Wikipedia: Buddhism in Japan
William E. Deal & Brian Ruppert, A Cultural History of Japanese Buddhism (2015)

note: The Nihon shoki dates the gift to 552; the Gangōji engi and Jōgū Shōtoku hōō teisetsu give 538, which many historians prefer. Marker near Kinmei's palace at Shikishima (Sakurai). No Wikidata item exists for the event.

summary.en: Built in the Silla capital Gyeongju during the reign of Queen Seondeok, this bottle-shaped tower of about 360 granite blocks is often called the oldest surviving astronomical observatory in East Asia, though its exact function is still debated.
summary.zh: 瞻星台建于新罗善德女王在位时的都城庆州，由约360块花岗岩砌成瓶形塔身，常被称为东亚现存最古老的天文台，但其确切用途至今仍有争议。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Gyeongju Historic Areas
一然《三国遗事》卷1 善德王知几三事
Wikipedia: Cheomseongdae

note: The Samguk yusa places it in Seondeok's reign (632–647); the Sejong sillok jiriji gives 633 (Zhenguan 7), and 647 is also cited.

summary.en: Japan's oldest poetry anthology gathers about 4,500 poems by emperors, courtiers, frontier guards and commoners, written with Chinese characters used for their sounds (man'yōgana). Its latest datable poem is from 759, and Ōtomo no Yakamochi is thought to have been its main compiler.
summary.zh: 《万叶集》是日本现存最古老的和歌集，收录天皇、贵族、戍边防人和平民的约4500首和歌，以借汉字表音的“万叶假名”书写。其中可确定年代的最晚一首作于759年，一般认为大伴家持是主要编纂者。

sources.title: Britannica: Man'yō-shū
Wikipedia: Man'yōshū
Ian Hideo Levy (trans.), The Ten Thousand Leaves: A Translation of the Man'yōshū (1981)

note: Compiled after 759; the collection probably reached its final form in the 780s.

summary.en: Commissioned by King Seonjo in 1596 and completed by the royal physician Heo Jun in 1610, this 25-volume compendium organised East Asian medicine for Korean use and was printed in 1613. It was reprinted in China and Japan and is on the UNESCO Memory of the World Register.
summary.zh: 《东医宝鉴》由宣祖于1596年下令编纂，御医许浚于1610年完成，1613年刊行。这部25卷的医学全书将东亚医学系统整理以适合朝鲜之用，曾在中国和日本翻刻，已列入联合国教科文组织《世界记忆名录》。

sources.title: UNESCO Memory of the World: Donguibogam: Principles and Practice of Eastern Medicine
Wikipedia: Donguibogam

summary.en: Over three days a fire driven by strong winds burned most of Edo, including the main keep of Edo Castle, and killed perhaps 100,000 people. The shogunate rebuilt the city with firebreaks, wider streets and relocated temples and daimyo mansions; the keep was never rebuilt.
summary.zh: 强风助长下的大火连烧三日，焚毁江户大半城区，包括江户城天守阁，死者或达10万人。幕府重建时设置防火带、拓宽街道，并迁移寺院和大名宅邸；天守阁此后再未重建。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Great Fire of Meireki
Wikipedia (ja): 明暦の大火
Jeffrey Hanes, "Urban Planning as an Urban Problem", in J. L. McClain et al. (eds.), Edo and Paris (1994)

note: Began on the 18th day of the 1st month of Meireki 3 (2 March 1657, Gregorian). Death estimates range from about 30,000 to over 100,000.

summary.en: Nine days before the Tokyo Olympics opened, Japanese National Railways began services on the world's first high-speed railway, between Tokyo and Shin-Ōsaka, at up to 210 km/h. The 'bullet train' cut the journey from about 6.5 to 4 hours and inspired high-speed rail worldwide.
summary.zh: 东京奥运会开幕前九天，日本国有铁道开通了东京至新大阪之间的世界首条高速铁路，最高时速210公里。“子弹列车”将行程由约6个半小时缩短为4小时，并带动了全球高速铁路的发展。

sources.title: Britannica: Shinkansen
Central Japan Railway Company: About the Shinkansen
Wikipedia: Tokaido Shinkansen

note: Journey time fell to 4 hours at opening and to 3 hours 10 minutes in November 1965.
